Interface Wifi

All Known Implementing Classes:
NativeWifi
public interface Wifi
Wi-Fi connection control. ArduinoUno.getWifi() is the board's own radio, which the compiler lowers to the Arduino board networking stack (WiFiS3 on UNO R4 WiFi, WiFiNINA on UNO WiFi Rev2, Arduino_RouterBridge on UNO Q); the UNO R3 has no radio of its own, so it gets its Wi-Fi from ArduinoWifiShield.getWifi() (the retired Arduino WiFi Shield's legacy WiFi library) instead. A unit test passes mock(Wifi.class). Get it once, at startup, and pass it to the classes that need it.

ssid/password may be string literals or stable runtime strings returned by a SecretStore or another board-side configuration source. This keeps credentials out of firmware.

  • Method Details

    • begin

      void begin(String ssid, String password)
      Starts station-mode Wi-Fi on UNO R4 WiFi. On UNO Q, Wi-Fi belongs to Linux and must already be configured through App Lab or nmcli; this method initializes the MCU-to-Linux bridge and ignores the credential arguments.

    • beginAP

      void beginAP(String ssid, String password)
      Starts the board as a Wi-Fi access point named ssid, so a phone or laptop can join it directly (typically to serve a provisioning page through HttpServer). On UNO R4 WiFi, password is a WPA2 passphrase of at least 8 characters, or empty for an open network; call localIP(int[]) after status() reports STATUS_AP_LISTENING to obtain the access point's address. On UNO Q the MCU cannot create an access point: Linux owns Wi-Fi, so the hotspot must already be running (nmcli device wifi hotspot ssid <ssid> password <password>); this method only initializes the MCU-to-Linux bridge, ignores both arguments, and status() reports STATUS_CONNECTED once the bridge is up.

    • status

      int status()

    • localIP

      void localIP(int[] octets)
      Writes the board's current IPv4 address into octets (caller-owned, at least 4 entries), one byte value (0-255) per element, most significant first — e.g. 192, 168, 1, 45. When status() reports STATUS_AP_LISTENING, this is the access point's address; when it reports STATUS_CONNECTED, it is the station address. UNO Q's current router API does not expose either address and writes four zeroes. Juno has no heap, so there is no String-returning form here — print each octet with Serial.print(int) and a literal "." between them.

    • gatewayIP

      void gatewayIP(int[] octets)
      Writes the IPv4 address of the router the board is connected to (its gateway) into octets (at least 4 entries), in the same form as localIP(int[]). Only meaningful once status() reports STATUS_CONNECTED; a gateway that does not share the board's subnet usually means a bad DHCP lease. UNO Q's router API does not expose it and writes four zeroes.

    • macAddress

      void macAddress(int[] octets)
      Writes the Wi-Fi interface's six-byte hardware (MAC) address into octets (at least 6 entries), one byte value (0-255) per element, most significant first; print them in hex to compare against a router's client list. UNO Q's router API does not expose it and writes six zeroes.
